questions.q: What are the two purchasing models Azure SQL Database offers?
questions.explain: Both models answer the same question — how much compute, memory, and I/O — with different units and different control.

questions.q: What are the three service tiers under the DTU model?
questions.explain: The DTU model bundles compute, memory, and I/O into a single number across these three tiers.

questions.q: What are the three service tiers under the vCore model?
questions.explain: The vCore model prices compute and storage separately across these three tiers.

questions.q: Which purchasing model is required to apply Azure Hybrid Benefit (bringing an existing SQL Server license)?
options: Either model works identically for Hybrid Benefit
questions.explain: Because vCore prices compute and storage separately, it's the model that supports applying an existing license to reduce the compute cost.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why is 'which tier do I pick' not really a single question?
options: Because compute options apply equally to both DTU and vCore models
Because Azure SQL Database only offers one tier regardless of model
Because service tiers are chosen automatically by Microsoft with no user input
Because it involves choosing a purchasing model (DTU or vCore), then a service tier within that model, and for vCore, also a compute option (provisioned or serverless)
questions.explain: This lesson sets up Lesson 9 (purchasing model) and Lesson 10 (compute option) as the two follow-on decisions.
